headline: Anthropic’s preliminary S-1 reports rapid growth alongside compute financing exposure
summary: Anthropic’s October 26, 2026 preliminary Form S-1 reports $11.6 billion in revenue and $1.0 billion in operating income for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $787 million in revenue and a $1.2 billion operating loss in the same 2025 quarter. The filing says consumption-based services made up 80% of first-half 2026 revenue and 48% of revenue came through cloud-provider marketplaces. It reports $112.4 billion in cash and $19.3 billion in short-term investments at June 30, 2026; the six-month 2026 figures are unaudited. The filing also describes multi-year minimum-purchase and take-or-pay compute obligations, a shift toward leased accelerators and dedicated facilities, and conditional infrastructure financing. The filing describes capacity up to $42 billion under a Broadcom arrangement for 2026 lease obligations, up to $30 billion from Google (none issued by June 30, 2026), and up to $20 billion from Amazon; separately, it reports $10.2 billion aggregate principal of notes issued to two accredited investors by the filing date. These facility ceilings do not establish cash drawn, amounts paid or compute delivered. Several aggregate compute-commitment totals are left blank in the preliminary filing. Large reported net losses include non-cash fair-value remeasurement of convertible notes and related instruments. These disclosures describe the company’s reported results and financing structure; they do not establish compute utilization, future revenue, total realized compute cost or a completed IPO.
